full_judgment: 8. The learned lower Court, on the basis of the evidence on record, decreed the suit with a finding that the suit land originally belonged to Mehammad Ali, the grand-father of the father of the plaintiff and that there was no diluvion and the suit land was althrough under possession of the plaintiff. The defendant preferred an appeal against that judgment and decree of the trial Court before the court of the District Judge, Chittagong. The appeal was numbered as Other Appeal No.66 of 1982. It was heard and disposed of by the Subordinate Judge, First Court. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed the appeal on the grounds that the suit was not maintainable in view of the provisions of sub-section (3) of section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950; that the suit was barred by limitation because it was not filed within 6 years from the publication of PS khatian and from the date of knowledge of the RS khatian; that the suit land was vague and that the suit was bad for defect of parties as all the co-sharers of RSPS and BS khatians were not made parties in the suit. The plaintiff, by filing this revisional application challenged the validity of the decisions arrived at by the learned appellate Court.
